processing: A green tea from Mount Emei; the detailed method is not well documented, and as with other premium greens of the mountain the leaf is unoxidised and picked young.
harvest_season: Early spring. The name refers to picking before Qingming, while snow may still lie on the mountain.
appearance_dry: Described only as fresh and clear in colour; young, tender leaf is typical of the class.
appearance_liquor: Clear and pale; a light yellow-green is typical of tender Mount Emei greens.
appearance_wet: Not well documented; small, tender shoots are typical of the class.
taste_profile: A clean fragrance and a pure, mellow cup.

brewing.notes: General advice for tender Mount Emei greens: cool the water first and keep the first steep brief.

vintage_note: Sold in spring as a current-harvest green, with pre-Qingming lots at the top, as is usual for greens of this class. Since it is a brand as well as a tea name, packaged grades are set by the company rather than by a public standard.
description:
Emei Xueya, whose name means Emei snow sprout, is a green tea from Mount Emei and one of the best-known names of the mountain alongside Zhu Ye Qing. The name is explained by a story: monks going out to pick before Qingming with spring snow still on the ground.

Today the name belongs largely to a business. It is sold by a company associated with the listed tourism group that runs Mount Emei, so most of what you meet is branded and packaged rather than village tea.

It is described as clean and fragrant, pure and mellow, which fits the wider Mount Emei style. Details of how it is made are not published in any depth, so treat it as a tender spring green and brew it with cool water and short steeps.

Buy by harvest date and grade. If you are comparing Sichuan greens, tasting it next to Zhu Ye Qing is the obvious test, since the two share a mountain and compete for the same shelf.
history:
Monks picking in the snow make a good story, but it should be read as a legend, and claims of an unbroken temple tea reach further than the evidence.

The documented story is commercial. The brand entered the market in 2007, and by 2011 its sales were close to 100 million yuan, with its parent company, Emei Shan A, planning to make tea a major part of its business. Press reports at the time placed it behind Zhu Ye Qing, the provincial leader.
